title: CrackMorph-XAI-Net: A Topology-Preserving and Explainable Framework for Automated Crack Morphology
summary: Automated crack inspection is increasingly recognized as a critical component of infrastructure monitoring; however, cracks continue to be reported primarily as binary segmentation masks by many current vision-based systems. While localization is facilitated by such masks, limited structural information is provided for robust engineering interpretation. For practical crack assessment, measurable morphological features -- including centerline geometry, branching behavior, junction locations, topology, and severity-related indicators -- are required.
